sanskrit_verse:
गुणवानिति यः प्रोक्तः ख्यापितो जनसंसदि ।
कथं तेनैव वक्त्रेण निर्गुणः परिकथ्यते ॥
transliteration: guṇavān iti yaḥ proktaḥ khyāpito janasaṃsadi / kathaṃ tenaiva vaktreṇa nirguṇaḥ parikathyate //
sph_interpretive_translation: One who has been declared virtuous and established in public discourse cannot, by that very same declaration, be spoken of as devoid of virtue.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derived from established social recognition
Causation through consistency of declarative acts
Capacity-based responsibility grounded in prior affirmations
Restoration logic based on reversal of false attribution
Consciousness alignment via congruence of word and identity
executable_legal_axioms: IF a person is publicly affirmed as possessing a quality THEN any contradictory assertion by the same affirmer is null
IF a speaker establishes another's character THEN that speaker is bound to maintain logical continuity in subsequent declarations
IF a contradiction occurs without contextual shift THEN the initial affirmation overrides the latter negation
IF a person’s capacity is acknowledged THEN denial of that capacity by the same recognizer incurs automatic invalidity
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, when a witness or party has previously affirmed the integrity or capability of an individual in formal proceedings, subsequent denials of that same attribute by the same source are legally non-operative unless accompanied by verifiable contextual transformation. The threshold of responsibility lies in maintaining cognitive and declarative coherence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality requires that speech acts carry forward their own epistemic weight; inconsistency arises not for punishment but for correction. Anupūrvaśaḥ indicates that prior declarations condition subsequent ones. Proportional responsibility aligns with the continuity of consciousness-expression. The non-punitive reality rule holds that contradiction reflects misalignment rather than fault deserving penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Require the contradictor to re-affirm the original declaration in public forum
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Oblige the speaker to clarify context or withdraw contradiction
Capacity Restoration: Reconnect the speaker with the basis of their earlier affirmation
Integrity Reintegration: Facilitate harmonization between past and present statements through conscious review
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. Virtue once affirmed cannot be unspoken except by conscious correction. Justice serves restoration, not retribution. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
